sources.name: JPL SBDB close approaches to Earth and the Moon
sources.licence: NASA/JPL SBDB Close-Approach Data API, public domain U.S. government work. https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/cad.api. Distances are AU. The training counts use approaches within 0.05 AU. The lookahead file also keeps interstellar approaches out to 1 AU.

sources.name: JPL fireball and bolide reports
sources.licence: NASA/JPL Fireball Data API, public domain U.S. government work. https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/fireball.api. Radiated energy is in units of 10^10 joules. Impact energy is an estimate in kilotons of TNT.

sources.name: JPL Sentry impact-risk list
sources.licence: NASA/JPL Sentry API, public domain U.S. government work. https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/sentry.api. A current snapshot, not a historical series.

sources.name: JPL SBDB designations and first observations
sources.licence: NASA/JPL Small-Body Database Query API, public domain U.S. government work. https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb_query.api. first_obs is the discovery control for close-approach counts.

sources.name: CelesTrak SATCAT decay dates
sources.licence: CelesTrak SATCAT redistribution of the public satellite catalog. https://celestrak.org/pub/satcat.csv. Cite CelesTrak (T.S. Kelso). Decay dates record reentries that have already happened.
